source_excerpt: At an age when most children are still learning to string sentences together, a toddler from Karnataka is already making a name for herself on the tabla. Swarshri Hegde, who is just 2 years and 10 months old, has found a place in the India Book of Records for reciting and playing 12 taals on the instrument. A video of her performance, shared on X, has gone viral and drawn heartfelt reactions from netizens across the country.A young prodigy from Uttara KannadaSwarshri hails from Honnavara in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka. Her record-setting feat involves both reciting and playing 12 taals on the tabla, a combination that usually takes years of patient practice to master. Reciting a taal means vocalising its bols, the syllables that represent each stroke, while playing it demands precise control of rhythm and hand movement.Also Read: 4-ingredient candy bar fudge: An easy homemade treat without refined sugar, dairy, butter or oilWhy the feat stands outIn Indian classical music, a taal is a repeating rhythmic cycle that forms the backbone of a performance. Each cycle has a fixed number of beats, a pattern of divisions and a point at which the cycle returns to its starting beat, known as the sam. Learning even one taal requires a strong sense of timing, memory and concentration. Managing a dozen of them, both in speech and on the instrument, is an achievement for a student of any age, which makes it all the more remarkable for a child not yet three.Here's the video:Netizens shower praiseThe clip has struck a chord on social media, with many users expressing pride and admiration for the little artist.
